study.question: Does a field-pair summary benefit when its temporal location follows the magnitude of target-conditioned content contributions, rather than treating every matching event equally?
study.hypothesis: The incumbent occupancy representation uses O=mu_uniform*S where S is the signed DIN-weighted pair content and mu_uniform is the unweighted mean of the temporal-bin rank basis on the exact pair support. This can locate a strongly activated recent contribution at the mean position of many weak earlier matches. Replacing only mu_uniform by mu_abs=sum(abs(stopgrad(w))*c)/sum(abs(stopgrad(w))) on that same support may better bind location to the evidence represented by S. Absolute weight means contribution magnitude, not positive preference. This is a provisional representation hypothesis, not an established mechanism.

nearest_work.difference: Archived v4 primary text lines80-85 and271-277 describes target-conditioned local activation and unnormalized weighted sum pooling. We inherit signed unnormalized content; only a pair-specific temporal centroid uses positive magnitudes. Normalizing centroid coordinates does not normalize DIN content. This limited reading does not establish novelty of weighted positional summaries.

Pinned benchmark implementation lines221-255 uses repeated sequence encoding, query decoding and boosting. We keep the current one-step token interaction and replace one statistic before interaction; no per-layer sequence encoder or query decoder is introduced. Its original paper detail is unavailable in the authorized archive, so original-method comparison remains incomplete.

The candidate inherits the entire incumbent and changes only the centroid supplied to its existing zero-start pair-rank bank. No new parameters or tokens. A uniform configuration reproduces its intended function.

The unsuccessful marginal-centroid candidate replaced true pair location by estimates from single-field marginals. This study retains exact joint pair support and reweights events within that support using already available activation magnitudes.

study.proposed_difference: Inside _select_pair_rank_component only, construct detached positive magnitudes abs(w) on exact joint pair support. Divide by the pair maximum when positive, then divide the weighted rank sum by the positive mass; these two normalizations preserve the absolute-weight centroid while avoiding a signed denominator and an arbitrary epsilon threshold. All-zero magnitude falls back to the uniform centroid; empty support has zero centroid. Replace O=mu_uniform*S with O=mu_abs*S and retain signed S and its gradient. No gradient passes through centroid weights; this deliberately tests a content-conditioned summary without adding a second direct optimization path through local activation. Both centroids are computed in the candidate and optional uniform preflight configuration. Every other inherited path is retained.
predictions: Conditional on all host preflights, magnitude placement improves validation macro AUC against g0-r0017-pair_rank_occupancy and its exact replay g0-r0018-pair_centroid_joint_replay. Report macro Logloss and all four task AUC/Logloss deltas even if macro AUC improves.

For constant absolute activation on nonempty pair support, the two centroids coincide. A singleton with nonzero weight has its exact rank; all-zero weights use uniform fallback. These are algebraic checks, not empirical mechanism evidence.

The magnitude centroid remains inside the minimum/maximum temporal coefficient on pair support; changes outside pair support cannot change it. Padding IDs and target action cannot influence it through the inherited sanitization boundary.

falsifiers: A valid run ties or loses macro AUC to the incumbent: no predictive support for this implementation under the frozen protocol. Do not conclude that all contribution-conditioned placement mechanisms are refuted.

The production helper violates convex-hull, constant-magnitude, zero-support, masking or scale/sign invariance, or the uniform configuration fails parent replay: implementation/comparison invalid; fix before interpreting performance.

An apparent gain does not survive a future admissible paired-seed comparison, or is explained by numerical/RNG mismatch, actual parameter changes or a changed information boundary: mechanism support remains absent.

A gain only establishes this specific coupled replacement in one seed; absent a gradient-path control and larger representation controls, it cannot establish a general advantage for weighted temporal centroids.
alternative_explanations: Activation magnitudes can be poorly calibrated or dominated by negative contributions, so counting every matched event equally may be the more robust placement statistic.
The new centroid may encode activation concentration or content dependence rather than improved temporal alignment; task/slice gains cannot by themselves separate these explanations.

Detaching centroid weights changes the trained representation while preventing its direct gradient path. A future differentiable-centroid control would be required to distinguish representation value from optimization effects.
The existing first-moment and feedback paths may already encode all useful placement information; adding content conditioning at this compression stage may be redundant.

nc,oc=classes(new),classes(old)
for name in ['FeedbackMemory','JointBlock']:
 assert ast.dump(nc[name])==ast.dump(oc[name])
methods=lambda c:{n.name:n for n in c.body if isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef)}
nm,om=methods(nc['Model']),methods(oc['Model'])
changed=[k for k in nm if ast.dump(nm[k])!=ast.dump(om[k])]
assert changed==['__init__','_pair_rank_tokens','_select_pair_rank_component'],changed
init=copy.deepcopy(nm['__init__'])
idx=next(i for i,a in enumerate(init.args.args) if a.arg=='pair_placement_source')
default_idx=idx-(len(init.args.args)-len(init.args.defaults))
init.args.args.pop(idx);init.args.defaults.pop(default_idx)
init.body=[n for n in init.body if not (isinstance(n,ast.If) and ('pair_placement_source' in ast.unparse(n.test) or "pair_rank_component != 'occupancy'"==ast.unparse(n.test))) and not (isinstance(n,ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(t,ast.Attribute) and t.attr=='pair_placement_source' for t in n.targets))]
assert ast.dump(init)==ast.dump(om['__init__'])
rank=copy.deepcopy(nm['_pair_rank_tokens'])
for n in ast.walk(rank):

config=ast.literal_eval(next(n.value for n in new.body if isinstance(n,ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(t,ast.Name) and t.id=='CONFIG' for t in n.targets)))

for k,v in config.items():assert sig[k]==v or list(sig[k])==v,(k,v,sig[k])
# A tiny one-dimensional stand-in executes the exact production helper for
# one batch/window/pair at a time. It does not validate torch broadcasting,
# autograd, devices, BF16 or full-model execution.
class V:
 def __init__(self,x):self.x=list(x) if isinstance(x,(list,tuple)) else [x]
 def op(self,o,f):
  o=o if isinstance(o,V) else V(o)
  size=max(len(self.x),len(o.x));assert len(self.x) in (1,size) and len(o.x) in (1,size)
  return V([f(self.x[i%len(self.x)],o.x[i%len(o.x)]) for i in range(size)])
 def __mul__(self,o):return self.op(o,lambda a,b:a*b)
 __rmul__=__mul__
 def __truediv__(self,o):return self.op(o,lambda a,b:a/b)
 def __sub__(self,o):return self.op(o,lambda a,b:a-b)
 def __gt__(self,o):return self.op(o,lambda a,b:a>b)
 def __getitem__(self,k):return self
 def float(self):return self
 def detach(self):return self
 def abs(self):return V([abs(a) for a in self.x])
 def sum(self,**kw):return V(sum(self.x))
 def amax(self,**kw):return V(max(self.x))
 def clamp_min(self,a):return V([max(a,b) for b in self.x])
def where(c,a,b):
 size=max(len(c.x),len(a.x),len(b.x))
 return V([a.x[i%len(a.x)] if c.x[i%len(c.x)] else b.x[i%len(b.x)] for i in range(size)])
mock=SimpleNamespace(where=where,ones_like=lambda x:V([1.]*len(x.x)))
fn=copy.deepcopy(nm['_select_pair_rank_component'])
module=ast.Module(body=[fn],type_ignores=[]);ast.fix_missing_locations(module)
ns={'torch':mock};exec(compile(module,'production_helper','exec'),ns)
helper=ns[fn.name]
rng=random.Random(20262027);cases=0
for trial in range(1000):
 length=rng.randint(1,100)
 mask=[rng.random()<.35 for _ in range(length)]
 rank=[rng.uniform(-2,2) for _ in range(length)]
 weights=[rng.uniform(-3,3) for _ in range(length)]
 if trial%7==0:mask=[False]*length
 if trial%11==0:weights=[0.]*length
 if trial%13==0:weights=[(-1.)**i*2. for i in range(length)]
 if trial%17==0:weights=[w*1e-30 for w in weights]
 if trial%19==0:weights=[w*1e30 for w in weights]
 content=[rng.uniform(-3,3) for _ in range(7)]
 selected=[i for i,m in enumerate(mask) if m]
 uniform=sum(rank[i] for i in selected)/max(len(selected),1)
 mass=math.fsum(abs(weights[i]) for i in selected)
 weighted=math.fsum(abs(weights[i])*rank[i] for i in selected)/mass if mass else uniform
 for source,mu in [('uniform',uniform),('magnitude',weighted)]:
  model=SimpleNamespace(pair_placement_source=source,pair_rank_component='occupancy')
  out=helper(model,V([.2]*7),V(content),V(mask),V(rank),V(weights)).x
  assert all(math.isclose(a,mu*c,rel_tol=1e-11,abs_tol=1e-12) for a,c in zip(out,content))
  if selected:assert min(rank[i] for i in selected)-1e-12<=mu<=max(rank[i] for i in selected)+1e-12
  # Out-of-pair weights have no effect, including sign and scale changes.
  altered=[w if mask[i] else 1e35 for i,w in enumerate(weights)]
  out2=helper(model,V([.2]*7),V(content),V(mask),V(rank),V(altered)).x
  assert out==out2
  cases+=1
